text:
Sasha R: Ran a ~60s Nsight capture on the 8xA100 run that regressed yesterday. attaching the summary: https://internal/nsv/2170055555 and nvprof excerpt. main symptoms: long tail at the end of forward pass, spikes at collective edges.

Kevin L: saw the trace, looks like a 'collective drag' not pure compute. the last 2 ranks are waiting ~7-10ms on the final grad allgather.

Maria T: is KV-cache warmup causing uneven sequence lengths? iirc we had a burst of short prefix hits + sudden full-token requests which can blow up batch packing.

Ashley P: ran the microbench harness on the same model w/ deterministic batching. results:
- baseline (old kernel picker): 38.2 ms/token avg, tail p99=62ms
- new picker (heuristic favoring fp16 matmul on long seq): 36.8 ms/token avg, tail p99=59ms
But when enabling eager kv-prefetch we see tail drop to 48ms p99.

perf-bot: Regression detector: 2169999990 -> 2170055000: +9.2% p99 latency on multi-gpu TFwd flows. Linked traces: https://ci/perf/regressions/2170055555

Sasha R: Key questions: (1) is the tail from all-reduce serialization or scheduling skew? (2) does kernel selection policy amplify imbalance? (3) can batching heuristics avoid the mixed-short-long batch that widens the tail?

Kevin L: hypothesis: comm/compute overlap lost because some ranks choose a fallback matmul kernel that has lower single-GPU latency but worse progress when mixed with asynchronous launches. i.e., kernel variance increases rendezvous time.

Maria T: +1. i replayed with nvprof and added our custom timers. snippet of the timer output:
```
TIMERS: rank0 forward_compute 13.4ms, allreduce_wait 8.7ms, kv_prefetch 0.8ms
TIMERS: rank6 forward_compute 14.9ms, allreduce_wait 17.3ms, kv_prefetch 1.0ms
```
we see rank skew on the allreduce_wait at the end.

Ashley P: i instrumented kernel-selection logs (added --kernel-annotate). interestingly, ranks with higher allreduce_wait selected cuBLAS fp32 GEMM for chunk sizes > 2048, others used our fused-gemm-q4 kernel. that mixture correlates with the wait spikes.

Sasha R: so mixed kernel types + heterogeneous sequence lengths = rendezvous amplification. can we force homogeneous kernel families per collective to reduce variance?

Kevin L: we can try a circuit-breaker: if any rank in a node falls back to non-fused kernel, force all ranks on that node to the compatible fallback for that step. cheap to implement in runtime routing.

Maria T: for batching heuristics, proposal: decouple short-prefix packing from long full-token requests by having a two-queue packer with max-mix ratio. when a long request arrives, avoid stuffing it with many short items. reduces variance in forward time.

Ashley P: microbench results for two-queue strategy (8gpu synthetic):
- single queue: avg 37.9ms, p99 64.5ms
- two-queue (max-mix 0.2): avg 38.6ms, p99 50.2ms
tradeoff: small avg increase but big tail win.

runtime-eng: logistically, we need a small AB test on staging with real traffic. steps:
1) runtime build with kernel-circuit-breaker flag ON
2) packer variant rollout in traffic-sim groups (10% -> 50% -> 100%)
3) collect timers + Nsight lightweight 10s snapshots across nodes
4) compare p50/p90/p99 and allreduce tail distribution

Sasha R: I'll open an RFC PR with the experimental configs and attach the command lines. example run flags: 
```
--runtime.kernel_policy=circuit_breaker_on
--batcher.strategy=two_queue
--batcher.max_mix=0.2
--telemetry.custom_timers=on
```
I'll also add an nvprof-friendly capture hook for the 2 ranks with highest allreduce_wait.

Kevin L: for analysis, please include a small script to compute per-collective skew:
```
# pseudo
skew = max(allreduce_waits) - min(allreduce_waits)
if skew > 5ms: mark_step_as_skewed
```
that'll help quantify the impact.

Maria T: one more thing: KV-cache prefetch. i suggest delaying prefetch for short-prefix-only batches so that prefetch doesn't starve compute on other ranks. small change: if majority in batch are short, set prefetch=off.

Ashley P: will run a combined experiment: two-queue packer + circuit-breaker + kv-prefetch-adaptive. hoping for <5% avg change and >20% p99 reduction. i'll push test harness results by EOD.

perf-bot: Perf test queued: job/2170055600 (two-queue + cb + kv-adaptive). ETA 45m.

Sasha R: awesome. if the AB shows wins, next step is to add kernel-family affinity in the collective scheduler (low-risk change). thanks all, will update thread with results and traces. :thumbsup:
